explanations.answer: Return to the LORD and obey His voice
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moses, Israel's leader, says they and their children “…return to the LORD your God and obey His voice with all your heart and all your soul…” So the kids are in on it too. That's a whole family turning around together, like a car full of people finally agreeing to pull over and ask for directions.

explanations.answer: Build a new altar in that far land
explanations.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader, doesn't say a word about an altar here. What he says is that they and their children return to the LORD their God and obey His voice. It's a turning back of the heart, not a building project. I bet nobody even had to pick up a hammer.

explanations.answer: Send messengers back to find Moses
explanations.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader, never says they go looking for him. He says they remember all these words, and then they and their children return to the LORD their God and obey His voice. The words they carry with them are enough. No messengers, no search party, just a people turning back.

explanations.answer: Gather them from all the nations
explanations.explanation: Right on target. Moses says the LORD “…will restore you from captivity and have compassion on you and gather you from all the nations…” Compassion is right there in the middle of it. I love how personal that is, because He is the One doing the gathering.

That's not what Moses says. He says the LORD will restore them from captivity and have compassion on them. The same people who were scattered are the ones He gathers. Nobody gets swapped out on this team.

explanations.answer: Send them a new king out there
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't mention a king at all in these verses. He says the LORD will restore them, have compassion on them and gather them from all the nations. The LORD Himself does the gathering. No crown required.

Moses says the opposite. He says the LORD “…will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will take possession of it.” Then comes the part that makes this one a no-brainer: “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” So it's more, not less. Think of a batch that comes out of the oven bigger than the recipe promised.

Yes, False. Moses says the LORD will bring them into the land their fathers possessed. Then he says, “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” So they end up with more than their fathers, not less. That's the kind of math I like.

explanations.answer: Love Him with all their heart and soul
explanations.explanation: Yes! Moses says the LORD “…will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, and you will love Him with all your heart and all your soul, so that you may live.” The LORD does the heart work, and the love follows. And it's "so that you may live," so it all points toward life.

explanations.answer: Forget every curse they ever heard
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say they forget anything. Back in verse 1, he has them calling these words to mind. What he says after the LORD circumcises their hearts is that they will love Him with all their heart and all their soul, so that they may live.

explanations.answer: Never wander from the land again
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't promise that here. What he says is that once the LORD circumcises their hearts, they will love Him with all their heart and all their soul, so that they may live. That love is the result he names. I'll stick to what he said.

explanations.answer: On the enemies who hate and persecute them
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Moses says, “Then the LORD your God will put all these curses upon your enemies who hate you and persecute you.” So the curses end up on the ones who hate and persecute them. Quite a turn of events.

explanations.answer: On the leaders who led them astray
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't mention leaders who led anyone astray here. He says the LORD will put all these curses upon the enemies who hate Israel and persecute them. That's where the curses land in this verse.

explanations.answer: On the wilderness they once crossed
explanations.explanation: No wilderness in this verse. Moses says the LORD will put all these curses upon Israel's enemies, the ones who hate them and persecute them. The curses land on people, not on a stretch of sand.

Delight, yes! Moses says, “…the LORD will again delight in your prosperity, as He delighted in that of your fathers…” The word "again" matters, because it's something that happened before. A word like delight tells you how the LORD feels about His people.

Moses says the opposite. The word is delight: “…the LORD will again delight in your prosperity, as He delighted in that of your fathers…” It's a happy picture, with the LORD delighting in what He gives them. No grieving in that line.

Share is a nice word, but it's not Moses' word here. He says the LORD will again delight in their prosperity, just as He delighted in that of their fathers. The verse is about how the LORD feels about it. Delight is the word he uses.

True. Moses says the LORD will make them abound “…if you obey the LORD your God by keeping His commandments and statutes that are written in this Book of the Law, and if you turn to Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” Both pieces go together: what's written and a heart turned toward Him. A recipe card doesn't help much if you never turn on the oven.

This one is actually True. Moses says the LORD will make them abound “…if you obey the LORD your God by keeping His commandments and statutes that are written in this Book of the Law…” He adds that they turn to Him with all their heart and with all their soul. So the Book of the Law is right there in the verse.
Moses says the opposite. He says, “For this commandment I give you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach.” Not too difficult, not out of reach. It's meant to be within their grasp.

That's right, False. Moses says, “For this commandment I give you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach.” It's within their grasp. I wish every instruction manual I've ever met could say that.

explanations.answer: In their mouth and in their heart
explanations.explanation: Yes. Moses says, “But the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it.” Nobody has to climb or sail anywhere to get it. It's already close enough to say out loud and carry inside.

explanations.answer: With the priests in the tabernacle
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't point to the priests or the tabernacle here. After saying it's not in heaven and not beyond the sea, he says, “…the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart…” It's close to the people themselves.

explanations.answer: With the elders at the city gate
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't send anyone to the elders or the city gate. He says the word is very near them, in their mouth and in their heart. It's right where they are.

explanations.answer: Love the LORD and walk in His ways
explanations.explanation: That's the life side. Moses says, “For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances…” Love comes first in that list. The rest follows from it.

explanations.answer: Gather gold and build strong cities
explanations.explanation: Gold and strong cities aren't in Moses' command. He says he commands them to love the LORD their God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances. His list is about loving and walking with the LORD.

explanations.answer: Offer a sacrifice every single morning
explanations.explanation: A daily sacrifice isn't what Moses names here. He says he's commanding them today to love the LORD their God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances. That's the life side as he describes it.

True. Moses says, “For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances, so that you may live and increase…” Living and increasing are the goal he states. He also says the LORD may bless them in the land they're entering to possess.

This one is True. Moses says he's commanding them to love the LORD their God and keep His commandments, “…so that you may live and increase…” He also says the LORD may bless them in the land. So that purpose is stated right in the verse.

That's what Moses declares. He says, “…you will surely perish; you shall not prolong your days in the land…” It's a serious line, and I think it hits hard. That's why he follows it with such a clear invitation to choose life.

Moses doesn't mention flocks in that warning. He declares that they will surely perish and that they shall not prolong their days in the land they're crossing the Jordan to possess. It's a heavy line. I think Moses is being honest because he wants them to see the road clearly.

explanations.answer: They will wander forty more years
explanations.explanation: Forty more years isn't in Moses' words here. He declares that if they turn away to other gods, they will surely perish and they shall not prolong their days in the land. It's a heavy part of the passage. I think Moses says it plainly so they can see what's at stake.

Right. Moses says, “I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing.” That's about as big a witness stand as you could ask for. And it all leads into his next words: “Therefore choose life…”
The elders aren't the witnesses here. Moses says, “I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today…” He calls on heaven and earth themselves. The witness stand is as big as it gets.

Moses doesn't name the priests or the Levites here. He says, “I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing.” His witnesses are heaven and earth.

That's it. Moses says, “Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live…” The choice reaches past the people in front of him to the generations after them. A fresh batch of dough today turns into cookies someone else gets to enjoy.
Moses doesn't limit it to the elders and leaders. He tells all Israel, “Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live…” That's the people and the generations after them.
Moses doesn't name the nations around them here. He says, “Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live…” The ones who live are Israel and their descendants.
Yes. Moses says, “For He is your life…” That's the reason behind loving the LORD, obeying Him and holding fast to Him. I think that's one of the sweetest lines in the whole sermon.
Judge isn't the word Moses uses here. After telling them to love the LORD, obey Him and hold fast to Him, he gives the reason: “For He is your life…” That's how he describes the LORD to them.
Shield isn't the word in this verse. Moses wants them to love the LORD, obey Him and hold fast to Him. Then he says, “For He is your life…” That's the reason he gives.
